meta.mechanism: PCSK9 inhibitor (humanized monoclonal antibody, ~3% murine sequence in the antigen-binding CDR); prolongs hepatic LDL receptor lifespan, lowers LDL-C ~55-60% early, attenuated over time by antidrug antibodies
meta.indication: prevention of major adverse cardiovascular events in high-risk patients (prior cardiovascular event or high-risk primary prevention) on background lipid-lowering therapy with LDL-C >=100 mg/dL or non-HDL-C >=130 mg/dL

n_randomized.quote: Before the sponsor terminated the two trials, 16,817 patients had enrolled in SPIRE-1 and 10,621 had enrolled in SPIRE-2
n_randomized.note: Table 1: bococizumab N = 5312, placebo N = 5309. Registry S3 enrollment (actual) 10,564 = FAS (5281 bococizumab, 5283 placebo), which excludes patients who attempted to randomize more than once and all patients at site 3027 (quality-related event).

median_followup.quote: At the time of trial termination, the median follow-up time was 7 months in SPIRE-1 and 12 months in SPIRE-2.
median_followup.note: Follow-up truncated: all patients followed for events until November 1, 2016, events adjudicated by February 20, 2017.

inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Must have an LDL C \>/=100 mg/dL (2.6 mmol/L) OR non HDL C \>/=130 mg/dL (3.4 mmol/L).

SPIRE-2 allowed no statin in patients with complete statin intolerance.

planned_events.quote: the trial sample size for SPIRE-2 (11,000 patients for an anticipated 508 patients with an adjudicated and confirmed primary end point) would provide approximately 90% power to detect a 25% relative risk reduction in the trial primary end point.
planned_events.note: Observed 403 primary events (79% of the planned 508) when the sponsor stopped the trial.

stopped_early.quote: The trials were stopped early after the sponsor elected to discontinue the development of bococizumab owing in part to the development of high rates of antidrug antibodies, as seen in data from other studies in the program.

biomarker_effects.quote: At 12 weeks, patients who received bococizumab had a reduction of 54.2% in the LDL cholesterol level from baseline, as compared with an increase of 1.0% among those who received placebo (absolute between-group difference, -55.2 percentage points).
biomarker_effects.note: 4300 patients, follow-up up to 12 months. Published the same day as the outcome results (2017-03-17), so not available before readout. 'high-titer antidrug antibodies developed in a substantial proportion of the patients who received bococizumab, which markedly diminished the magnitude and durability of the reduction in LDL cholesterol levels.'

biomarker_effects.quote: Compared with placebo, bococizumab 150 mg Q14 days reduced LDL-C at week 12 by 53.4 mg/dl and bococizumab 300 mg Q28 days reduced LDL-C by 44.9 mg/dl; this was despite dose reductions in 32.5% and 34.2% of subjects at week 10 or 8, respectively.
biomarker_effects.note: Phase 2, n=354 on statin, LDL-C >=80 mg/dL (NCT01592240). Percent change NOT FOUND in abstract. Model predicted 72.2 mg/dL without dose reductions. Published 2015-02-12, before readout.

hr.quote: In the higher-risk, longer-duration trial (in which the patients had a baseline LDL cholesterol level of ≥100 mg per deciliter [2.6 mmol per liter] and the median follow-up was 12 months), major cardiovascular events occurred in 179 and 224 patients, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.97; P=0.02).
hr.note: Registry S3 (FAS, 5281 vs 5283): HR 0.79 (0.65-0.97), log-rank p = 0.021469; rates 3.33 vs 4.19 per 100 participant-years. Key secondary (nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, CV death) HR 0.74 (0.60-0.92), P=0.007. CV death HR 0.82 (0.50-1.36); all-cause death HR 0.91 (0.63-1.32). Companion SPIRE-1: HR 0.99 (0.80-1.22); pooled SPIRE-1+2: HR 0.88 (0.76-1.02), P=0.08.

safety_signals.value: Injection-site reactions much more frequent with bococizumab: 10.4% vs 1.3% (combined SPIRE-1+2)
safety_signals.quote: Injection-site reactions were more common in the bococizumab group than in the placebo group (10.4% vs. 1.3%, P<0.001).
safety_signals.note: Table 4: incidence rate ratio 8.33 (6.99-9.92); injection-site irritation IRR 4.71. Combined trials, not SPIRE-2 alone.

safety_signals.value: Immunogenicity: antidrug antibodies in nearly half and neutralizing antibodies in 29% of bococizumab patients in the SPIRE lipid-lowering trials, attenuating LDL-C lowering
safety_signals.quote: In the SPIRE lipid-lowering program, antidrug antibodies developed in nearly half the patients who received bococizumab and neutralizing antibodies developed in 29%, which in some affected patients substantially attenuated LDL-cholesterol lowering over time.
safety_signals.note: Antidrug-antibody status in SPIRE-1/SPIRE-2 themselves was 'not yet known' at publication. Detail in S4.

safety_signals.value: Adverse events leading to drug discontinuation more frequent: 6.3 vs 4.2 per 100 patient-years (IRR 1.49)
safety_signals.quote: Adverse events leading to drug discontinuation were more frequent in the bococizumab group than in the placebo group
safety_signals.note: Table 4: 684 (6.3) vs 466 (4.2), IRR 1.49 (1.33-1.68). Serious adverse events similar: IRR 0.99 (0.93-1.06).

safety_signals.value: No excess new-onset diabetes or cataract; small rise in glucose, no change in HbA1c
safety_signals.quote: Reports of newly diagnosed diabetes and of cataracts were similar in the two groups and did not vary according to the magnitude of the reduction in LDL cholesterol levels.

genetics.finding: PCSK9 nonsense (loss-of-function) mutations in ARIC black participants associated with 28% lower LDL-C and 88% lower CHD risk; a variant in whites with 15% lower LDL-C and 47% lower CHD risk
genetics.effect: HR 0.11 (0.02-0.81) blacks; HR 0.50 (0.32-0.79) whites over 15 years
genetics.quote: Of the 3363 black subjects examined, 2.6 percent had nonsense mutations in PCSK9; these mutations were associated with a 28 percent reduction in mean LDL cholesterol and an 88 percent reduction in the risk of CHD

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: PCSK9 and HMGCR variants give near-identical CV protection per unit LDL-C lowering
genetics.effect: OR 0.81 (0.74-0.89) per 10 mg/dL lower LDL-C for PCSK9 score
genetics.quote: Variants in PCSK9 and HMGCR were associated with nearly identical protective effects on the risk of cardiovascular events per decrease of 10 mg per deciliter (0.26 mmol per liter) in the LDL cholesterol level: odds ratio for cardiovascular events, 0.81 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.89) for PCSK9

genetics.finding: LDL-C is causal; CTT meta-analysis: major vascular events reduced ~22% per 1 mmol/L LDL-C reduction (benchmark for calculator)
genetics.quote: similar proportional reductions in major vascular events per 1·0 mmol/L LDL cholesterol reduction were found in all types of patient studied (rate ratio [RR] 0·78, 95% CI 0·76-0·80; p<0·0001)

consensus_explanation.summary: SPIRE-2 met its primary end point: bococizumab reduced major cardiovascular events by 21% (179 vs 224 events; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.65-0.97, P=0.02) in high-risk patients with LDL-C >=100 mg/dL, but the margin was narrow because the sponsor stopped the trial early (median follow-up 12 months, 403 of 508 planned events). The investigators and the ACC read the result as support for the LDL/PCSK9 hypothesis rather than for the drug: the size of the benefit fits what a ~57% (about 1.9 mmol/L) placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction over about one year predicts, and in the pooled SPIRE data benefit was larger with greater LDL-C lowering and longer treatment. The caveats are why the drug failed even though the trial succeeded. Bococizumab is humanized, and antidrug antibodies (in nearly half of patients, neutralizing in 29% in the lipid trials) attenuated and varied LDL-C lowering (SPIRE-2 placebo-adjusted -56.8% at 14 weeks, -43.2% at 52 weeks) and caused frequent injection-site reactions (10.4% vs 1.3%). The companion lower-risk, shorter SPIRE-1 trial was null (HR 0.99) and the pooled HR was 0.88 (0.76-1.02, P=0.08). Pfizer ended the programme on 1 November 2016 for immunogenicity, attenuation and commercial reasons, without unblinded outcome data, so the early stop was a non-scientific decision that truncated an otherwise informative trial.

open_questions: Readout date choice: Pfizer's 2016-11-01 release (S5) announced discontinuation and the halt of SPIRE-1/SPIRE-2 but disclosed no outcome results, and the sponsor and investigators had no unblinded outcome data at that time (S1). The first public SPIRE-2 outcome result was the ACC.17 presentation, ACC press release and NEJM online publication on 2017-03-17, which is used as readout_date. No Pfizer press release on the outcome results was found.

Outcome label: SPIRE-2's own primary end point was met (HR 0.79, 0.65-0.97, P=0.02), so the label is success. The SPIRE programme as a whole was not: SPIRE-1 HR 0.99 and pooled HR 0.88 (0.76-1.02, P=0.08), and the drug was abandoned. Whether SPIRE-2 had a prespecified alpha split or multiplicity adjustment with SPIRE-1 is not stated in the main text; the integrated pooled analysis plan was written after discontinuation but before unblinding.
Alpha: not stated in S1 main text; 0.05 two-sided assumed from registry two-sided 95% CIs and log-rank test.

Which LDL-C effect to use: placebo-adjusted -56.8% (-73.8 mg/dL, -1.91 mmol/L) at 14 weeks vs -43.2% at 52 weeks (absolute 52-week value not reported for SPIRE-2). Calculator inputs use the 14-week value, the only one with a reported absolute change. The time-averaged effect over the 12-month median follow-up lies between the two, so the 14-week value overstates the exposure.
Antidrug-antibody status inside SPIRE-1/SPIRE-2 was not known at publication (S1); the ~48% ADA / 29% neutralizing figures come from the six lipid-lowering trials.
Absolute apoB and non-HDL-C changes NOT FOUND (Supplementary Appendix not accessed).
Registry FAS (10,564) differs from the NEJM randomized count (10,621) because the FAS excludes duplicate randomizations and site 3027; HR is identical (0.79, 0.65-0.97).
ACC press release URL read directly; a Wayback Machine snapshot could not be checked because archive.org was offline on 2026-10-23.
